Design reassessment: normal Ready application staging is pure/private until actual Disk.commit file-sync/rename/directory-sync. Persisted/applied events, outward messages and advance follow successful IO. Configuration mutations remain deferred; on application-write failure the node is poisoned and messages are not exposed. LightReady applies separately, without inventing a mandatory commit-index fsync. OpenRaft vote/log IO is serialized, flush success follows actual persistence and application/snapshots retain applied/membership tuples. Recovery clearance is blocked by SEC03. Compatible tenant/key batches are explicitly distinguished from a physical cluster; quorum KMS is NOT_MODELED and actualKMS0. Offered first-dirty timers, natural final drain, encoded/logical queues and aggregate history/sample/group caps are now explicit and checked. Normal source/credential/network/cgroup/known-CID isolation is preserved, but SEC01/SEC02 prevent complete resource-boundary clearance.

findings.reproduction: With TEMP=TMP=D:\codex\2026-11-01\task\test-temp and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, run python -B D:\codex\2026-11-01\task\M02.10_R1_SECURITY_REPRO.py. The lifecycle section mocks an exited direct leader while the selector still owns a descendant-held pipe, then expires the deadline. The actual bounded() finally branch closes the pipes/selector but calls killpg zero times and wait zero times. This is source reachability, not live native execution. The function serves Cargo metadata and protoc probes, including ordinary host CI.
findings.expected: Deadline/output failure must terminate the owned group even after its leader exits. Preserve the primary failure and perform finite group TERM/grace/KILL/reaping. Outer Docker containment cannot replace the promised subcommand lifecycle cleanup.
findings.observed: The entire group cleanup is guarded by process.poll() is None. If the leader has already exited, an owned descendant retaining the pipes survives refusal. A leader that exits on TERM also prevents later KILL of a TERM-ignoring descendant. The error is detected but group cleanup is omitted.

findings.reproduction: Run root M02.10_R1_SECURITY_REPRO.py under task-local TEMP/TMP/no-bytecode. Valid descriptors claim one byte; fake Docker cp writes exactly2MiB to the owned destination before returning. Actual copy_bundle, object_controller.copy_artifacts and native_capture.copy each permit that allocation, then refuse its size. Receipt records2,097,152 host bytes before refusal at each boundary, beyond1MiB/file; all fixtures were removed normally. Docker was mocked and no real resource was touched.
findings.expected: Enforce actual source type/size and aggregate host allocation during transfer, before writing over-quota files. Guest descriptors are untrusted hints. Use bounded bytes/header admission or equivalent streaming enforcement, reject directory/link substitutions and preserve uncertain resource state.
findings.observed: native_controller.copy_bundle:123, object_controller.copy_artifacts:71 and native_capture.copy:81 invoke docker cp directly to disk, then inspect completed bytes. Docker.command stdout bounds do not bound cp payloads. Oversized or directory source data can consume the host artifact quota before refusal; finite guest8/18GiB scratch caps do not enforce host1MiB/file or32MiB/artifact limits.
